# Manually rotate static role credentials

The LDAP secrets plugin can rotate LDAP credential for static roles configured
the plugin.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [set up an `ldap` plugin](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/setup). 
- You have permission to update LDAP credentials in Vault.

</Tip>

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

@include 'ldap/rotate-creds/cli.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

@include 'ldap/rotate-creds/api.mdx'

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

These steps apply to root-managed and self-managed static roles. Your policy
must grant `read` on `<mount>/static-role/<name>` to open the role and `update`
on `<mount>/rotate-role/<name>` to rotate its credentials. The GUI hides
**Rotate credentials** when you do not have the rotation permission.

1. Open the Vault GUI, go to **Secrets engines**, and select your LDAP mount.

1. Open the **Roles** tab and select the static role.

1. Click **Manage**, then **Rotate credentials**.

1. In the **Rotate credentials?** dialog, click **Confirm**. Manual rotation
   restarts the role's rotation period.

The GUI displays **Credentials successfully rotated.** after a successful
rotation. If you have already revealed the password on the details page, the
GUI refreshes it after rotation. Otherwise, it does not fetch the password
until you ask to see it.

To view the rotated credentials, click **Get credentials**. Your policy must
grant `read` on `<mount>/static-cred/<name>` for this action.

</Tab>
